definition: The Artificial Intelligence Cold War (AI Cold War) is a narrative in which geopolitical tensions between the United States of America (USA) and the People's Republic of China (PRC) could lead to a Second Cold War waged in the area of artificial intelligence technology rather than in the areas of nuclear capabilities or ideology.
details: The context of the AI Cold War narrative is the AI arms race, which involves a build-up of military capabilities using AI technology by the US and China and the usage of increasingly advanced semiconductors which power those capabilities. According to a February 2019 publication by the Center for a New American Security, General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party Xi Jinping – believes that being at the forefront of AI technology will be critical to the future of China's global military and economic power competition.

explainer.lead: The Artificial Intelligence Cold War is a way of describing US–China rivalry over artificial intelligence, especially its military uses and the advanced semiconductors that power it. It matters because leadership in AI is linked to future military and economic power, raising the stakes of technological competition.

tiers.eli5: Imagine two countries racing to build the smartest machines and the powerful computer parts those machines need. Each worries that falling behind could weaken its military and economy. Calling this an “AI Cold War” compares that rivalry to a Cold War, but the contest centers on AI rather than nuclear weapons or ideology.
tiers.practitioner: This is a geopolitical framing rather than an engineering method or a measurable technical condition. For engineers, it provides context for work involving military AI capabilities and the advanced semiconductors needed to run them. A pitfall is treating the label as evidence of an actual declared war or assuming that technical progress alone determines the rivalry.
tiers.paperLevel: The AI Cold War is a narrative in which US–PRC geopolitical tensions could produce a Second Cold War centered on artificial intelligence rather than nuclear capabilities or ideology. Its stated context is an AI arms race: military AI build-ups coupled with increasingly advanced semiconductors. A February 2019 Center for a New American Security publication reported Xi Jinping’s view that AI leadership would be critical to China’s future military and economic competition; the narrative supplies no formal metric or threshold for identifying such a Cold War.

explainer.example: If the US and China each expand AI-enabled military capabilities and seek more advanced semiconductors to run them, the AI Cold War narrative reads these linked efforts as strategic rivalry. The concern is not only who has better technology, but how that lead could affect military and economic power.

usedIn.name: Military AI development
usedIn.detail: The US and China build military capabilities using AI technology.

usedIn.name: Advanced semiconductors
usedIn.detail: Increasingly advanced chips power the AI capabilities at the center of the rivalry.

usedIn.name: Geopolitical analysis
usedIn.detail: The narrative frames AI competition in terms of future military and economic power.

explainer.intuition: The central idea is that AI can become a strategic arena of great-power rivalry, much as nuclear capabilities and ideology were central to the original Cold War. Competition over military AI and the chips behind it is therefore interpreted as part of a broader struggle for power.
howItWorks: Geopolitical tension between the United States and China provides the backdrop.
Both countries build up military capabilities that use AI technology.
Increasingly advanced semiconductors supply the computing power for those capabilities.
AI leadership is linked to future military and economic strength, turning the build-up into a Cold War narrative.
explainer.whyItMatters: The narrative connects AI development to national security, economic competition, and dependence on advanced semiconductors. It also highlights how fear of falling behind can feed an AI arms race.
misconceptions: It is a narrative about possible conflict, not the name of a declared war.
It does not describe competition over AI alone; advanced semiconductors are part of the build-up.
It is not limited to military strength, because economic power is also at stake.
